items.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: a fellow that I had worked with in Washington, D.C., at Ike’s Stockade, was a comic. His name was Buddy Bowser.

ctx.x: So again we’ll pick up where you’re just arriving for your stay in New York.

Well I stayed with a friend. I stayed with an uncle. My mother’s older brother, Nathaniel Bacon, was a dentist and his office was right about 137th, 138th and 7th Avenue. He lived in the Dunbar apartments but those apartments were very small and he had a wife and a son, my cousin, and there wasn’t a lot of room there so even though I was welcome to stay there, I only stayed briefly and moved in with this friend of my father’s who had a little more room, not a lot. All of this was temporary because I was looking…
Since you lived right next door to Minton’s, could you describe Minton’s, with the interior of Minton’s and also on a given night, what was the clientele like, what was a night at Minton’s like?
